title: Projectiles and Variable Acceleration
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Projectiles Worksheets
standard_text: Model motion under gravity in a vertical plane using vectors (projectiles); use calculus in kinematics for motion in a straight line: v = ds/dt, a = dv/dt = d²s/dt².
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on projectiles (time of flight, greatest height, range) and variable acceleration using calculus. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Split the motion into horizontal (constant speed) and vertical (acceleration g).
body_html:
How it works

A projectile with speed u at angle θ: horizontal speed u cos θ (constant), vertical speed u sin θ − gt. Time of flight = 2u sin θ/g.

When acceleration is not constant, use calculus: v = ds/dt, a = dv/dt.

Example

s = t³ − 2t. Velocity at t = 2?

v = 3t² − 2

12 − 2

Answer: 10 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Using suvat when acceleration is not constant.
  • Using u cos θ for the vertical speed.
  • Forgetting that vertical speed is 0 at the top.

faq.q: How do you find the range of a projectile?
faq.a: Find the time of flight from the vertical motion, then multiply by the horizontal speed u cos θ.
Only when the acceleration is constant. Otherwise use calculus.
